title: Common Cold: Symptoms and Overview
content: The common cold is a mild viral infection of the nose and throat, most often caused by rhinoviruses. Typical symptoms include a runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, sore throat, mild cough, mild headache, and general tiredness. Fever is usually absent or very low-grade in adults, though children may run a higher fever. Symptoms typically build over 1-3 days, peak around day 3-5, and resolve within 7-10 days. Most colds do not require medical treatment and resolve on their own with rest and fluids.

title: Influenza (Flu): Symptoms and Overview
content: Influenza is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses. Unlike a cold, flu symptoms usually begin abruptly and are more severe: high fever (often 101-104F), chills, body aches, headache, fatigue that can be severe, dry cough, sore throat, and nasal congestion. Symptoms typically last about a week, though fatigue can linger longer. Most healthy people recover without complications, but flu can lead to serious complications like pneumonia in young children, older adults, pregnant women, and people with chronic conditions.

title: Migraine Headache: Symptoms and Overview
content: A migraine is a moderate to severe headache, often on one side of the head, described as throbbing or pulsing. Common accompanying symptoms include nausea, vomiting, and extreme sensitivity to light and sound. Some people experience an 'aura' beforehand - visual disturbances like flashing lights or zigzag lines. Attacks can last 4 to 72 hours if untreated. Common triggers include stress, certain foods, hormonal changes, lack of sleep, and bright lights. Migraines differ from tension headaches, which cause a dull, pressing pain on both sides of the head without nausea or light sensitivity.

title: Tension Headache: Symptoms and Overview
content: Tension-type headaches are the most common form of headache, causing a dull, aching sensation on both sides of the head, often described as a tight band around the head. Unlike migraines, tension headaches don't typically cause nausea, vomiting, or significant sensitivity to light. Common triggers include stress, poor posture, eye strain, dehydration, and lack of sleep. They usually respond well to rest, hydration, and over-the-counter pain relief.

title: Dengue Fever: Symptoms and Overview
content: Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne viral infection common in tropical and subtropical regions. Symptoms typically appear 4-10 days after being bitten and include sudden high fever, severe headache (often behind the eyes), muscle and joint pain (sometimes called 'breakbone fever'), nausea, vomiting, skin rash, and mild bleeding such as nosebleeds or bruising. Most cases resolve within 1-2 weeks, but a small percentage can progress to severe dengue, a medical emergency with warning signs like severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, and bleeding.

title: Malaria: Symptoms and Overview
content: Malaria is a mosquito-borne parasitic disease common in tropical regions. Symptoms usually appear 10-15 days after an infective mosquito bite and include high fever with chills and sweating (often in cycles), headache, muscle aches, fatigue, nausea, and vomiting. Fever patterns can be cyclical, recurring every 24-72 hours depending on the parasite species. Malaria is a medical emergency requiring prompt diagnosis and treatment, as it can progress rapidly to severe illness, especially in children and pregnant women.

title: Typhoid Fever: Symptoms and Overview
content: Typhoid fever is a bacterial infection (Salmonella Typhi) spread through contaminated food and water. Symptoms develop gradually over 1-3 weeks and include sustained high fever that rises in a stepwise pattern, headache, weakness and fatigue, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhea, and sometimes a rash of flat, rose-colored spots. Untreated typhoid can lead to serious complications, so prompt antibiotic treatment is important.

title: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI): Symptoms and Overview
content: A urinary tract infection is a bacterial infection anywhere in the urinary system. Common symptoms include a strong, persistent urge to urinate, a burning sensation when urinating, passing frequent small amounts of urine, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, and pelvic pain in women. If the infection spreads to the kidneys, symptoms can include fever, chills, back or side pain, nausea, and vomiting - this requires prompt medical attention.

title: Gastritis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Gastritis is inflammation of the stomach lining, often caused by infection (commonly H. pylori bacteria), excessive alcohol use, or long-term use of pain relievers like NSAIDs. Symptoms include a gnawing or burning pain in the upper abdomen, nausea, vomiting, a feeling of fullness after eating a small amount, bloating, and loss of appetite. Some people have no symptoms at all. Chronic untreated gastritis can increase the risk of stomach ulcers.

title: Food Poisoning: Symptoms and Overview
content: Food poisoning results from eating contaminated food, usually caused by bacteria, viruses, or parasites. Symptoms typically begin within hours to a few days of eating contaminated food and include nausea, vomiting, watery or bloody diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and sometimes fever. Most cases resolve within a few days with rest and fluids. Severe cases with high fever, bloody stool, signs of dehydration, or symptoms lasting more than three days need medical attention.

title: Asthma: Symptoms and Overview
content: Asthma is a chronic condition causing inflammation and narrowing of the airways. Common symptoms include shortness of breath, chest tightness, wheezing (a whistling sound when breathing), and coughing, often worse at night or early morning, or triggered by exercise, cold air, allergens, or respiratory infections. Symptom severity varies widely between people and can range from mild and occasional to severe and frequent, sometimes leading to asthma attacks that require emergency treatment.

title: Hypertension (High Blood Pressure): Symptoms and Overview
content: Hypertension is often called a 'silent' condition because it typically causes no noticeable symptoms, even when blood pressure readings are dangerously high. Most people find out they have high blood pressure through a routine check. In rare cases of very severe hypertension, symptoms can include severe headache, shortness of breath, nosebleeds, and chest pain. Because it's usually symptomless, regular blood pressure checks are the main way it's detected. Untreated, it raises the risk of heart disease and stroke.

title: Type 2 Diabetes: Symptoms and Overview
content: Type 2 diabetes often develops gradually and symptoms can be subtle at first. Common signs include increased thirst, frequent urination, increased hunger, unexplained weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision, slow-healing sores, and frequent infections. Some people have no noticeable symptoms for years before diagnosis, which is why routine blood sugar screening is important, especially for people with risk factors like obesity or a family history of diabetes.

title: Iron Deficiency Anemia: Symptoms and Overview
content: Iron deficiency anemia occurs when the body doesn't have enough iron to produce adequate hemoglobin. Common symptoms include fatigue and weakness, pale skin, shortness of breath, dizziness, cold hands and feet, brittle nails, headache, and a fast or irregular heartbeat. Symptoms often develop slowly and can be mild at first, worsening as the deficiency progresses. It's commonly caused by blood loss, poor dietary iron intake, or pregnancy.

title: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever): Symptoms and Overview
content: Allergic rhinitis is an allergic reaction causing inflammation of the nasal passages, triggered by allergens like pollen, dust mites, or pet dander. Symptoms include sneezing, runny or stuffy nose, itchy and watery eyes, itchy throat, and postnasal drip. Unlike a cold, allergic rhinitis doesn't cause fever and symptoms can persist for as long as the person is exposed to the trigger, sometimes lasting weeks during pollen seasons.

title: Sinusitis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Sinusitis is inflammation of the sinuses, often following a cold or due to allergies. Symptoms include facial pain or pressure (especially around the eyes, cheeks, and forehead), nasal congestion, thick nasal discharge (yellow or green), reduced sense of smell, headache, and sometimes mild fever. Acute sinusitis usually resolves within 2-4 weeks; symptoms lasting longer may indicate chronic sinusitis.

title: Conjunctivitis (Pink Eye): Symptoms and Overview
content: Conjunctivitis is inflammation of the thin membrane covering the white of the eye and inner eyelid, commonly caused by viral or bacterial infection, or allergies. Symptoms include redness in the eye, itchiness, a gritty feeling, discharge that may form a crust (especially with bacterial infection), and watery eyes. Viral conjunctivitis is highly contagious and often accompanies a cold. It usually resolves within 1-2 weeks.

title: Chickenpox (Varicella): Symptoms and Overview
content: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy, blister-like rash. Symptoms typically begin with mild fever, tiredness, headache, and loss of appetite, followed 1-2 days later by an itchy rash that starts as red spots, develops into fluid-filled blisters, and eventually crusts over. New spots can appear over several days, so the rash often shows spots at different stages simultaneously. Most cases in children are mild and resolve within 1-2 weeks.

title: Measles: Symptoms and Overview
content: Measles is a highly contagious viral infection. Early symptoms include high fever, cough, runny nose, and red, watery eyes, appearing 10-14 days after exposure. Small white spots (Koplik spots) may appear inside the mouth. A few days later, a red, blotchy rash typically starts on the face and spreads down the body. Measles can lead to serious complications like pneumonia and encephalitis, particularly in young children, making vaccination important for prevention.

title: Pneumonia: Symptoms and Overview
content: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, caused by bacteria, viruses, or fungi. Symptoms include cough (often with phlegm), fever, chills, shortness of breath, chest pain that worsens with breathing or coughing, fatigue, and in severe cases confusion (especially in older adults). Symptoms can range from mild to severe and develop over days. Anyone with high fever, difficulty breathing, or chest pain should seek medical attention promptly.

title: Bronchitis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Bronchitis is inflammation of the bronchial tubes that carry air to the lungs, often following a cold or flu. Acute bronchitis symptoms include a persistent cough (which may produce mucus), chest discomfort, mild fever, fatigue, and shortness of breath. The cough can linger for several weeks even after other symptoms resolve. Chronic bronchitis, a form of COPD, involves a persistent productive cough lasting at least three months over two consecutive years.

title: GERD (Acid Reflux): Symptoms and Overview
content: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) occurs when stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus. Common symptoms include heartburn (a burning sensation in the chest, often after eating or at night), regurgitation of food or sour liquid, difficulty swallowing, chest pain, chronic cough, and a sensation of a lump in the throat. Symptoms often worsen when lying down or bending over after meals.

title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS): Symptoms and Overview
content: IBS is a common disorder affecting the large intestine. Symptoms include abdominal pain or cramping (often relieved by a bowel movement), bloating, gas, and changes in bowel habits - either diarrhea, constipation, or alternating between both. Symptoms often flare up after eating certain foods or during stress and can vary significantly in severity between individuals. IBS doesn't cause permanent damage to the intestines but can significantly affect quality of life.

title: Hypothyroidism: Symptoms and Overview
content: Hypothyroidism occurs when the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough thyroid hormone. Symptoms develop gradually and include fatigue, unexplained weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, hair loss, constipation, muscle weakness, depression, and slowed heart rate. Because symptoms are often subtle and develop slowly, hypothyroidism can go undiagnosed for a long time; blood tests are needed to confirm diagnosis.

title: Hyperthyroidism: Symptoms and Overview
content: Hyperthyroidism occurs when the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone. Symptoms include unexplained weight loss despite normal or increased appetite, rapid or irregular heartbeat, increased sweating, nervousness or irritability, tremors in the hands, difficulty sleeping, and heat intolerance. Some people also experience an enlarged thyroid gland (goiter) or eye changes if caused by Graves' disease.

title: Kidney Stones: Symptoms and Overview
content: Kidney stones are hard deposits of minerals that form in the kidneys. Small stones may pass without symptoms, but larger stones can cause severe, sharp pain in the side and back, below the ribs, that may radiate to the lower abdomen and groin. Other symptoms include pain during urination, pink, red, or brown urine, nausea and vomiting, and frequent urge to urinate. Severe pain (renal colic) often comes in waves.

title: Gallstones: Symptoms and Overview
content: Gallstones are hardened deposits that form in the gallbladder. Many gallstones cause no symptoms. When they do, symptoms include sudden and rapidly intensifying pain in the upper right abdomen or center of the abdomen, pain between the shoulder blades or right shoulder, nausea, and vomiting, often triggered after eating fatty meals. If a stone blocks the bile duct, it can cause fever, jaundice (yellowing of the skin), and requires prompt medical attention.

title: Appendicitis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Appendicitis is inflammation of the appendix, a medical emergency requiring prompt treatment. Classic symptoms include pain that starts near the belly button and shifts to the lower right abdomen, worsening over hours, along with loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, low-grade fever, and abdominal swelling. Pain often worsens with movement, coughing, or pressing on the abdomen. Anyone with suspected appendicitis should seek emergency care immediately, as a ruptured appendix is life-threatening.

title: Osteoarthritis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Osteoarthritis is the most common form of arthritis, caused by the breakdown of joint cartilage over time. Symptoms include joint pain that worsens with activity and improves with rest, stiffness (especially after waking up or sitting for a while), reduced range of motion, a grating sensation when using the joint, and swelling around the joint. It most commonly affects the hands, knees, hips, and spine, and typically develops gradually over years.

title: Rheumatoid Arthritis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune condition causing the immune system to attack the joints. Symptoms include tender, warm, swollen joints (often symmetrically on both sides of the body), joint stiffness that is usually worse in the mornings and after inactivity, fatigue, fever, and loss of appetite. Unlike osteoarthritis, it commonly affects smaller joints first, such as those in the hands and feet, and can also affect other organs.

title: Depression: Symptoms and Overview
content: Depression is a mood disorder causing persistent feelings of sadness and loss of interest. Symptoms include persistent low mood, loss of interest or pleasure in activities once enjoyed, changes in appetite or weight, sleep disturbances (too much or too little), fatigue or low energy, feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, difficulty concentrating, and in some cases thoughts of death or suicide. Symptoms typically last at least two weeks and interfere with daily functioning. If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please seek immediate help from a crisis helpline or emergency services.

title: Anxiety Disorder: Symptoms and Overview
content: Anxiety disorders involve excessive worry or fear that is difficult to control. Symptoms include persistent worry, restlessness, feeling on edge, fatigue, difficulty concentrating, irritability, muscle tension, and sleep disturbances. Physical symptoms can include a racing heart, sweating, trembling, and shortness of breath. Symptoms are considered a disorder when they are excessive, persistent (typically most days for six months or more), and interfere with daily life.

title: Insomnia: Symptoms and Overview
content: Insomnia is difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or both, resulting in unsatisfying sleep. Symptoms include difficulty falling asleep at night, waking up during the night, waking up too early, not feeling well-rested after sleep, daytime fatigue, irritability, difficulty concentrating, and increased errors or accidents. It can be short-term (often triggered by stress) or chronic (lasting a month or more).

title: Vitamin D Deficiency: Symptoms and Overview
content: Vitamin D deficiency often causes no obvious symptoms, especially when mild. When symptoms do occur, they can include fatigue, bone pain, muscle weakness or aches, mood changes, and impaired wound healing. Severe, prolonged deficiency in children can cause rickets (soft, weak bones), and in adults can contribute to osteomalacia and increased fracture risk. Diagnosis typically requires a blood test since symptoms alone are often too vague to confirm deficiency.

title: Eczema (Atopic Dermatitis): Symptoms and Overview
content: Eczema is a chronic condition causing inflamed, itchy skin. Symptoms include dry, sensitive skin, intense itching (especially at night), red to brownish-gray patches (often on hands, feet, ankles, wrists, neck, and inside elbows and knees), small raised bumps that may leak fluid when scratched, thickened or scaly skin, and raw or sensitive skin from scratching. Symptoms often flare up periodically and can be triggered by irritants, allergens, stress, or weather changes.

title: Psoriasis: Symptoms and Overview
content: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune condition that speeds up skin cell growth, causing patches of thick, scaly skin. Symptoms include red patches of skin covered with thick, silvery scales, dry cracked skin that may bleed, itching, burning, or soreness, thickened or ridged nails, and stiff, swollen joints in some cases (psoriatic arthritis). Symptoms often come and go in cycles, flaring for weeks or months, then subsiding.

title: Vertigo: Symptoms and Overview
content: Vertigo is a sensation of spinning or dizziness, as if you or your surroundings are moving when they aren't. Common causes include inner ear problems like BPPV (benign paroxysmal positional vertigo), Meniere's disease, or vestibular neuritis. Symptoms include a spinning sensation, loss of balance, nausea, vomiting, and sometimes hearing changes or ringing in the ears (tinnitus), depending on the underlying cause. Episodes can last seconds to hours.

title: Sciatica: Symptoms and Overview
content: Sciatica refers to pain that radiates along the path of the sciatic nerve, from the lower back through the hips and buttocks and down each leg, usually affecting only one side. Symptoms include sharp, shooting pain, numbness or tingling, and muscle weakness in the affected leg. Pain often worsens with sitting, coughing, or sneezing. It's commonly caused by a herniated disc or bone spur compressing part of the nerve.

title: Gout: Symptoms and Overview
content: Gout is a form of arthritis caused by a buildup of uric acid crystals in a joint. Symptoms include sudden, severe joint pain (often the big toe), swelling, redness, and warmth in the affected joint, and intense tenderness - even light touch can be painful. Attacks often occur at night and can wake a person from sleep. Symptoms typically peak within 12-24 hours and gradually improve over days to weeks, even without treatment.
